In [[mathematics]] and [[probability]], the '''Borell–TIS inequality''' is a result bounding the probability of a deviation of the [[uniform norm]] of a centered [[Gaussian measure|Gaussian]] [[stochastic process]] above its [[expected value]].  The result is named for [[Christer Borell]] and its independent discoverers [[Boris Tsirelson]], [[Ildar Ibragimov (mathematician)|Ildar Ibragimov]], and [[Vladimir Sudakov]].  The inequality has been described as "the single most important tool in the study of Gaussian processes."<ref name="RFG">{{cite book
| chapter = Gaussian Inequalities
| title = Random Fields and Geometry
| series = Springer Monographs in Mathematics
| year = 2007
| publisher = Springer New York
| location = New York, NY
| pages = 49&ndash;64
| isbn = 978-0-387-48116-6
| doi = 10.1007/978-0-387-48116-6_2}}
</ref>

==Statement==

Let <math>T</math> be a [[topological space]], and let <math>\{ f_t \}_{t \in T}</math> be a centered (i.e. mean zero) [[Gaussian process]] on <math>T</math>, with

::<math>\| f \|_T := \sup_{t \in T} | f_t |</math>

[[almost surely]] finite, and let

::<math>\sigma_T^2 := \sup_{t \in T} \operatorname{E}| f_t |^2.</math>

Then<ref name="RFG"/> <math>\operatorname{E}(\| f \|_T)</math> and <math>\sigma_T</math> are both finite, and, for each <math>u > 0</math>,

::<math>\operatorname{P} \big( \| f \|_T > \operatorname{E}(\| f \|_T) + u \big) \leq \exp\left(  \frac{- u^2}{2\sigma_T^2} \right). </math>
Another related statement which is also known as the Borell-TIS inequality<ref name="RFG" /> is that, under the same conditions as above, 
::<math>\operatorname{P}\big(\sup_{t\in T}f_t>\operatorname{E}(\sup_{t\in T}f_t)+u\big) \le \exp\bigg(\frac{-u^2}{2\sigma_T^2}\bigg)</math>,
and so by symmetry
::<math>\operatorname{P}\big(|\sup_{t\in T}f_t-\operatorname{E}(\sup_{t\in T}f_t)|>u\big) \le 2\exp\bigg(\frac{-u^2}{2\sigma_T^2}\bigg)</math>.
